object_description: compact symmetrical school volume with glazed façades and atriums
design_condition: The compact replacement building is placed at the north-eastern edge facing the demolished structure, preserving the existing outdoor spaces and views while creating a new address along the access path.

positive.statement: The clear presence along the access path creates a new address for the school.

position.rationale: Northeastern building edge provides the most plausible visible address beside the access approach.

positive.statement: The concentration on a new building at the north-eastern end of the perimeter is correct.

position.rationale: Top view clearly shows a compact mass concentrated toward the northeastern perimeter.

positive.statement: The symmetrical floor plan and arrangement of the two stairwells are good organizationally and for earthquake safety.

position.target: symmetrical floor plan and two stairwells
position.rationale: Symmetric outer footprint is visible, while stairwell locations require an interior approximation.

positive.statement: The division into public uses on the first floor and classrooms on the other floors is logical.

position.rationale: Lower building band anchors the first-floor use at the visible front portion of the volume.

positive.statement: The contemporary floor plans largely meet the formulated requirements.

position.rationale: Upper elevation bands provide a plausible distributed anchor for classroom floors.

positive.statement: The interventions in the listed pavilion buildings are limited to the bare essentials.

position.rationale: The sampled building supports a broad internal-organization judgment without exposing plan details.

positive.statement: The new building impresses with its compact construction volume and simple insulation perimeter.

position.rationale: Existing pavilions are not distinguishable, so the estimate uses an offset site-edge location.

positive.statement: The proposal has construction costs in the medium range because of the compact building and selective interventions.

position.rationale: Dense rectangular elevations and a simple perimeter visibly establish the compact volume.

negative.statement: The large volume continues to obstruct views of the forest, leaving the status quo unchanged.

position.target: forest views obstructed by large volume
position.rationale: The substantial upper mass is clearly visible across all elevation views and occupies a broad site footprint.

negative.statement: The entrance corner is obstructed rather than furnished, and the closed rear façade harms the courtyard quality.

position.rationale: An approximate corner and courtyard-facing edge are anchored on the visible perimeter.

negative.statement: The connection between the new building and the elementary school playground should be critically questioned.

position.rationale: The southern front edge is the plausible interface for an exterior playground connection.

negative.statement: The glazed façades are perceived as a foreign body in the existing school complex.

position.rationale: Continuous sampled perimeter surfaces support an approximate facade anchor, though glazing is not individually resolved.

negative.statement: The day-school opening to the south could be more generous for the intended use.

position.rationale: The south-facing elevation constrains the opening to the lower front facade.

negative.statement: Without additional glass and shading measures, the risk of overheating remains.

position.rationale: The south facade is the most plausible exposed surface for overheating-related glazing concerns.

negative.statement: The building-technology concept appears rather complex in relation to future district heating and its shortened life cycle.

position.rationale: Technology complexity and heating compatibility are not spatially represented in the exterior point cloud.

negative.statement: The formal response to the existing building fails to recognize its qualities and necessities.

position.rationale: The visible isolated mass supports a broad formal comparison, without representing the existing building.
